record.field: Document an infrastructure deviation as a nonconformity in the management system. Use for deviations that need to be handled according to ISO processes — root cause analysis, corrective actions.

async def execute(title, description, minion="", service="", severity="minor"): """Create a nonconformity in the management system.
mgmtsystem.nonconformity has five required fields, four of them without a default (partner_id, responsible_user_id, manager_user_id, origin_ids, plus description). All must be set or create() raises NotNullViolation. They are derived here rather than demanded: an infrastructure deviation is real even when no customer, employee or origin is obvious, so the tool must never be blocked by missing data. """ Nonconformity = env.get("mgmtsystem.nonconformity") # env.get() returns an EMPTY recordset for an installed model, and # bool(empty recordset) is False — so `if not Nonconformity` would fire # even though the model exists. Test the model name instead. if "mgmtsystem.nonconformity" not in env: return "ERROR: mgmtsystem.nonconformity model not available"
nc_description = description context = [] if minion: context.append(f"Affected machine: {minion}") if service: context.append(f"Affected service: {service}") if severity: context.append(f"Severity: {severity}") if context: nc_description += "\n\n--- Infrastructure Context ---\n" + "\n".join(context)
# partner_id is required. An infrastructure deviation has no customer, # so fall back to the company partner. partner = env.company.partner_id or env.user.partner_id
# responsible_user_id is required. The person documenting the deviation # (whoever is on duty) is the responsible party. responsible = env.user
# manager_user_id is required. Derive it from the responsible user's # hr.employee manager when hr is available; otherwise fall back to the # responsible user so the record can still be created. manager = responsible # Same empty-recordset trap as above: test the model name, not truthiness. if "hr.employee" in env: employee = env["hr.employee"].search([("user_id", "=", responsible.id)], limit=1) if employee and employee.parent_id and employee.parent_id.user_id: manager = employee.parent_id.user_id
# origin_ids is required. Use the reusable infrastructure origin, created # by data/nonconformity_origin_data.xml; create it if missing. Origin = env["mgmtsystem.nonconformity.origin"] origin = Origin.search([("ref_code", "=", "infrastructure_alert")], limit=1) if not origin: origin = Origin.create({ "name": "Driftavvikelse", "ref_code": "infrastructure_alert", })
nc = Nonconformity.create({ "name": title, "description": nc_description, "partner_id": partner.id, "responsible_user_id": responsible.id, "manager_user_id": manager.id, "origin_ids": [(6, 0, origin.ids)], })
return f"Nonconformity documented: {nc.name} (ID: {nc.id})"
